reason: E1 notes weak temperature dependence of yield strength in Mo-containing NbMoTaW and NbMoTaVW, supporting the premise that Mo contributes to high-temperature strength retention, but it does not provide evidence that adding Mo to TiVNbTa will preserve ductility or single-phase stability; the ductility and phase-stability premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mo addition to refractory HEAs promotes high-temperature strength retention
Mo-containing HEAs (e.g., MoNbTaW-based) show weak temperature dependence of yield strength
Solid-solution strengthening from Mo increases lattice distortion and impedes dislocation motion at high temperature
TiVNbTa baseline has yield strength ~330 MPa and compressive strength ~423 MPa at 1273 K
Mo addition will not compromise ductility or phase stability of TiVNbTa
